prompt: Which species can act as a nucleophile?
markscheme: **B.** A nucleophile donates a lone pair; NH₃ has one. H⁺, NO₂⁺ and BF₃ are electron-pair acceptors (electrophiles).

prompt: Write an equation for the reaction of bromoethane with aqueous sodium hydroxide, and identify the nucleophile and the leaving group.
markscheme: CH₃CH₂Br + OH⁻ → CH₃CH₂OH + Br⁻ **(A1)**; nucleophile OH⁻, leaving group Br⁻ **(A1)**

prompt: Distinguish between heterolytic and homolytic fission of a covalent bond.
markscheme: Heterolytic: both bonding electrons go to one fragment, forming ions; homolytic: one electron to each fragment, forming radicals **(A1)**

prompt: Define an electrophile and give one example.
markscheme: A species that accepts an electron pair to form a new bond, e.g. H⁺, NO₂⁺, Br₂ (polarised), or a carbocation **(A1)**

prompt: Explain why alkenes undergo electrophilic addition, and describe the bromine water test.
markscheme:
The C=C double bond, especially the π bond, is a region of high electron density that attracts electrophiles **(R1)**

Bromine water is decolourised (orange to colourless) by an alkene **(A1)** as bromine adds across the double bond, e.g. forming 1,2-dibromoethane from ethene **(A1)**
**A.** BF₃ (electron-deficient boron) accepts the lone pair donated by NH₃, forming a coordination bond. No proton is transferred, so it is not a Brønsted–Lowry reaction.

prompt: Explain why every nucleophile is a Lewis base and every electrophile is a Lewis acid.
markscheme: A nucleophile forms a bond by donating an electron pair — the definition of a Lewis base **(R1)**; an electrophile forms a bond by accepting a pair — a Lewis acid; the new bond is a coordination bond **(R1)**

prompt: In [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺, identify the ligand, explain how it bonds to Cu²⁺, and state the coordination number.
markscheme: Ligand H₂O donates a lone pair from oxygen to Cu²⁺, forming coordination bonds **(A1)**; coordination number 6 **(A1)**

prompt: Compare the mechanisms of hydrolysis of 1-bromobutane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane by OH⁻.
markscheme:
1-bromobutane (primary): SN2 — one step, OH⁻ attacks the carbon from the side opposite Br as Br⁻ leaves, through a transition state; rate $=k[\text{RBr}][\text{OH}^{-}]$ **(A2)**

2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary): SN1 — slow heterolysis to a tertiary carbocation, then fast attack by OH⁻; rate $=k[\text{RBr}]$ **(A1)**; tertiary carbocations are stabilised by alkyl groups, and steric hindrance blocks backside attack **(R1)**

prompt: Which halogenoalkane reacts fastest with aqueous hydroxide ions?
markscheme: **D.** The C–I bond is the weakest (longest), so iodide is the best leaving group and iodoalkanes react fastest — bond strength matters more than bond polarity here.

prompt: Outline the mechanism of the reaction between ethene and hydrogen bromide.
markscheme: The π electrons attack the δ+ H of H–Br; H–Br breaks heterolytically **(A1)**; a carbocation CH₃CH₂⁺ and Br⁻ form **(A1)**; Br⁻ donates a lone pair to the carbocation, forming bromoethane **(A1)**

prompt: Propene reacts with HBr to give mainly 2-bromopropane rather than 1-bromopropane. Explain this using carbocation stability.
markscheme:
Addition of H⁺ can give a secondary carbocation (CH₃CH⁺CH₃) or a primary one (CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺) **(A1)**

The secondary carbocation is more stable because two alkyl groups push electron density towards (stabilise) the positive carbon **(R1)**; it forms faster, so Br⁻ attacks it to give 2-bromopropane **(A1)**

prompt:
Benzene is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated nitric and sulfuric acids.

**(a)** Write the equation for formation of the electrophile. **[1]**

**(b)** Outline the mechanism and explain why benzene undergoes substitution rather than addition. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** HNO₃ + 2H₂SO₄ → NO₂⁺ + H₃O⁺ + 2HSO₄⁻ **(A1)**

**(b)** The delocalised π ring attacks NO₂⁺, forming a positively charged intermediate with broken delocalisation **(A1)**; loss of H⁺ restores the delocalised ring, giving nitrobenzene **(A1)**. Substitution keeps the stable delocalised system, whereas addition would destroy it **(R1)**
